title: Xbox CEO Plays Coy About Whether Elder Scrolls 6 Will Skip PlayStation
description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has suggested Microsoft could make more exclusive games again, but will The Elder Scrolls 6 be among them? We still don't know, but that's the question the BBC asked Sharma at Gamescom this week. But first, Sharma discussed her thoughts generally about exclusives, and how every platform, in her estimation, needs some form of exclusive content to grow. "We are increasingly going to be one of the largest platforms in the world. Every platform needs some form of exclusive experiences and content," she said. "And so, what we've shared is Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork [Revolution will be exclusive on console to Xbox]. We're going to do the best we can to continue to do that, all in context of the business being healthy, and so we have to balance that." Pressed to say if it is a "priority" to make The Elder Scrolls 6 exclusive to Xbox on console, Sharma smiled and said, "It's a beautiful game." Sharma recently visited the developers at Bethesda and offered an update on how the game was progressing. During her visit, protestors came to Bethesda's offices to drag Sharma for her decision to lay off thousands of Xbox developers, including people working on The Elder Scrolls 6. Due to these layoffs and other cuts, staffers at Bethesda are facing "crushing morale" and fears of more delays. In terms of Microsoft's approach exclusive games going forward, the team has said it will honor existing agreements for Xbox-made games that were previously announced as multiplatform releases. The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced in 2018, but at the time, Bethesda did not confirm platform details. Microsoft acquired Bethesda in 2021, and documents from the Microsoft vs. FTC case said The Elder Scrolls 6 was not planned for PS5. Former Xbox boss Phil Spencer, for his part, said in 2021 that making games exclusive to Xbox is "not about punishing any other platform." He also alluded to the possibility of The Elder Scrolls 6 being exclusive to Xbox. "In order to be on…

title: The Most Expensive Xbox Ever Sold Out, And People Are Already Flipping It For Thousands
description: Microsoft opened up preorders for its limited-edition 25th-Anniversary Xbox Series X, and within a minute, the most expensive Xbox ever sold out. While units will likely make their ways into the hands of Xbox fans with deep pockets, it looks like scalpers have also snatched up units, and as you'd expect, they're expecting to make a big payday by flogging them on sites like eBay. A quick look at the commerce platform reveals dozens of the rare Xbox Series X consoles have been listed, with prices ranging from $2,200 all the way up to an incredibly optimistic $27,426 by one seller in Australia--likely as a way to grab the top spot on eBay's search page. Microsoft opened up preorders with a $900 asking price for the console, so this is quite the jump. So far, it looks like quite a few of the consoles have been sold at the marked-up price, with several sales on eBay averaging between $1,900 to $2,300 per unit sold. That's a lot of cash for an Xbox! This is also an unpleasant reminder of the early years of the current console generation, as thanks to a semiconductor shortage, the Xbox Series X and the PS5 were hard to find. Scalpers using a variety of methods and programs were quick to snatch up restocks online and resold them, but supply chains eventually stabilized and access to the current console generation was easier--at least until a variety of factors saw their prices surge upwards last year, with no sign of relief in the immediate future. This is also yet another thing that scalpers have ruined, as many hobbies has been impacted by hustle culture. The Pokemon Trading Card Game has been especially hard hit, as every new restock at retailers usually sees scalpers buy up all of the available stock. Not even Pokemon donuts are safe, as the recent Krispy Kreme collaboration attracted plenty of people looking to make a quick buck. This is also yet another thing that scalpers have ruined, as many hobbies has been impacted by hustle culture. The Pokemon Trading Card Game…

title: Phantom Blade Zero’s New XR Glasses Actually Have Tiny Swords On Them
description: Phantom Blade Zero looks like it'll be a major highlight of the 2026 gaming calendar, as this blend of Chinese fantasy, swords, and sorcery is looking sharp. If you're looking to jump into the martial arts action of the Phantom World with a bit of style, then you can check out this new limited-edition version of the Viture Beast XR glasses when preorders open on August 27, priced at $599. Viture says they'll start shipping out on October 29, the same day that Phantom Blade Zero releases for PC and PS5. Preorder on Viture While the interior tech remains the same as the powerful XR specs, the exterior of the "Phantom Beast" glasses comes with tiny swords attached to them and a bundle of themed extras. Will the little blades help you fend off monsters in the Kungfu-punk world of Phantom Blade Zero? Probably not, but at least the 4.9-inch blades look cool. The design also features a splash of red and includes a unique carrying case that borrows several visual elements from Phantom Blade Zero. You'll find all the gear you need to customize the XR glasses for your face and the USB-C cable to connect them to your gaming devices, as well as the following exclusive Phantom Blade Zero items for this release: Mó Sanguine Blade Replica (12.5cm / 4.9 inches) Lens Cloth Game Art Card Brick Sticker Set As mentioned above, these have the same specs as the Viture Beast XR glasses that were released earlier this year. XR glasses have made some big strides over the last couple of years, and the Beast model packs an absurdly massive virtual display--the equivalent of a 174-inch screen--with an impressive number of features. The two Sony Micro-OLED screens offer a 1200p 120Hz display per eye; the glasses have five built-in display modes, real-time 3D conversion, and you can set the screen to follow your head movements or remain anchored in place. While it does have some chromatic aberration issues toward the edges, when you're focused directly on what's in front of you, these glasses…

title: Germany’s President Warns Of Downsides To Gaming, Including Games With “Extremist Ideologies”
description: This year's Gamescom event is underway in Cologne, Germany, and now the country's president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier--speaking at the event itself--warned people to consider the downsides to gaming. He also said gaming is great and has lots of positive effects on people and society. As reported by DPA International, he said video games have "become so ubiquitous," so it's only prudent to "discuss the downsides of this development." He said people should look at video games "objectively, honestly, and in a nuanced way." Steinmeier pointed out how the World Health Organization has warned of the dangers of gaming addiction, and he went on to say some video games expose people to "brutality and raw violence, to sexism, racism, inhuman thinking, and extremist ideologies." Also during his speech, Steinmeier said it's an outdated way of thinking to believe a "gamer" is someone who plays video games 24/7, eats junk food, and drinks energy drinks in a dark room. This "does not do justice to reality," he said. "Games have long since found their place at the heart of our society," he said, adding that advancements to gaming technology have helped various other industries, including medicine, architecture, and motor vehicle design. Gamescom 2026 kicked off with Geoff Keighley's Opening Night Live event, where a lot of announcements were made. The show itself is underway now, and for more, you can read GameSpot's interview with the organizers about how the biggest gaming event in the West continues to grow.

title: Zero Company Is The Rare Star Wars Game To Meaningfully Push A Genre Forward
description: Star Wars has been inspiring video games practically since video games have existed, but unlike the trailblazing film series, it has mostly been content to follow the leader. As a result, we've gotten all sorts of Star Wars video games molded after familiar templates, from first-person shooters to racing games. Those have been enjoyable enough, but they're very much defined as: "genre, but Star Wars." It's rare, but not unheard of, for a Star Wars game to push a genre forward with a combination of new ideas and great execution. Star Wars Zero Company is one such case. At first glance, it's easy to underestimate Zero Company, though. By all appearances this is simply XCOM, set in the world of Star Wars. You have a similar overhead perspective, commanding a small squad of commandos in turn-based combat as they take cover, flank and maneuver, and work together to take down formidable armies. And while that isn't inaccurate as shorthand, it would also sell the game short. Partly by capitalizing on the rich world of Star Wars itself, Zero Company finds ways to iterate further on XCOM, rather than merely imitate it. Burn, baby, burn First, some table-setting. Zero Company is set during the Clone Wars era of Star Wars, the tumultuous time seen in the prequel trilogy when the Republic was just on the verge of collapse into the Galactic Empire. Your player character, Hawks, is a down-and-out former Republic commander who started their own mercenary outfit after a disastrous mission gone wrong ruined their military career. The mercenaries, called Zero Company, are having money problems and struggling to find work, when a young Republic officer named Bennic offers steady, not-technically-Republic wet work in exchange for settling your debts. It would be easy to make Bennic sinister or conniving, dangling cash to desperate mercs, but this is one area where Zero Company excels. The characters are well-rounded and feel alive with humanity. Bennic is actually an honest broker for…

title: Peter Cullen, The Voice Behind Transformers’ Optimus Prime, Has Died
description: Actor Peter Cullen, best known as the booming voice of Optimus Prime in the Transformers franchise, has died at the age of 85. TMZ reported the news, which was corroborated by trade publications including The Hollywood Reporter. Cullen passed away peacefully in his Los Angeles home on Wednesday, according to his agent. Beginning his career as a live-action performer and an announcer, Cullen's run voicing Optimus Prime started with the original 1980s Transformers animated show. Optimus Prime was famously killed off in the 1986 Transformers film, and backlash led to the Autobots leader being resurrected in the show in 1987. It wasn't until 2007 with Transformers: The Game, a tie-in to the Michael Bay live-action film, that Cullen got to voice Optimus Prime in a video game project. Cullen would reprise the role in several other Transformers games, including the acclaimed Transformers: War for Cybertron and Platinum Games' Transformers: Devastation. Cullen even voiced the character when he debuted in Fortnite. Other than Optimus Prime, Cullen also voiced the chronically pessimistic Eeyore in several Winnie the Pooh films, shows, and video games. One of his more obscure video game credits is acting as the narrator in the 2019 puzzle game Crystal Crisis. Cullen's other iconic voice roles outside of Optimus Prime and Eeyore include the eponymous Predator in the original Predator film, Monterey Jack in Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers, and KARR in Knight Rider. He won a Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2023 Children's and Family Emmy Awards. It has been a tough week in the entertainment world, with many mourning the passings of Dolly Parton and Tim Curry, the latter whom had a small but memorable presence in video gaming.

title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Wants To Break Racing Games Out Of Their Comfort Zone
description: Great racing games have an x-factor that sets them apart from their peers, but you could argue that the genre hasn't meaningfully evolved over the decades. Star Wars: Galactic Racer aims to change that perception, as the new title from developer Fuse Games looks to other genres for inspiration. While it might look like a spiritual successor to 1999's Star Wars Episode 1: Pod Racer, Galactic Racer adds in some roguelite flavor and a dash of Burnout to its take on high-speed competition in a galaxy far, far away. "Our intention was actually to move the genre forward," Fuse Games CEO Matt Webster said to GameSpot. "We've made a lot of racing games in the past, and we love racing. This game came together because of a shared love of racing and Star Wars, but we needed to evolve. It needed to change; it needed to be something to push it forward and modernize it. It's probably the last sort of major genre that hasn't really had a transformative stealing of different types from different genres into racing." "And so, that's what we did here. We wanted to make a racing adventure where story and character are very important. But we've wrapped it up inside a runs-based structure. Runs-based games are games that are designed for infinite replayability, and we think racing thrives on replayability. Our assertion was that those things were going to be a great mix, and now, as that comes to life, people are coming for the Star Wars arcade racing action, but there's a boatload of depth in there." That all sounds like a fun recipe for single-player fun, but what about multiplayer? Online competition is a vital part of any racing game, and with a roguelite-influenced structure, you'd imagine that this wouldn't translate well to multiplayer racing. Fuse Games says that it has found a great balance for players who want to race against their fellow humans, as Galactic Racer's multiplayer leans heavy into the underworld aspect of Star Wars and allows you to place bets on how well you'll…

title: If You Thought Console Prices Were Too High, Things Could Get Even Worse
description: Video game console price increases could be back on the menu, as the Trump administration is reportedly weighing implementing a new round of tariffs on imported computer chips. According to Politico, the administration is considering expanding the number of tech products subject to the duties, and they could include everyday electronics that use these chips--including gaming consoles, data center servers, and laptops. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is reportedly aiming to use these tariffs to push foreign tech companies to build manufacturing plants inside the US if they want tax relief. While this plan hasn't been finalized and could change in the coming months, Politico's sources say that these new tariffs will be implemented slowly if they are approved. Tech companies have already warned that these taxes could backfire and hurt the US's efforts to win the artificial-intelligence race. The advanced chip factories required to produce crucial components like semiconductors and memory cost billions to establish and take years to build. This wouldn't be the first time that console prices have risen because of US President Donald Trump's tariffs, as Sony, Nintendo, and Microsoft hardware have all increased in price. While the companies haven't directly attributed the price hikes to tariffs--citing global economic instability and other factors as reasons their products became more expensive--they did directly mention that tariff refunds have helped their bottom line. Both Sony and Nintendo, for example, got nice little paydays earlier this year after the US Supreme Court declared Trump's tariffs to be unlawful. None of these refunds have been passed back to consumers, but the makers of the PlayDate handheld, Panic, confirmed this week that it'll be refunding anyone who bought the device when its price was increased to cover the tariffs.

title: GTA 6 Netflix Trailer’s Beefy Runtime Revealed, Footage Captured On PS5
description: At long last, Rockstar will lift the veil on GTA 6 today, August 27, via an "Extended Look" on Netflix. But how long will the broadcast be? Now we know. According to an updated listing for the showcase on the Netflix app, the Extended Look event will run for 26 minutes. That's pretty significant, but it should be, given Rockstar and Netflix are calling it "extended." This suggest it's more than a trailer but instead a proper deep dive into the world of GTA 6. That's exciting news for fans, as Rockstar has only delivered two trailers for the game since 2023, and only sparing other details along the way. Additionally, Netflix's blog post announcing the Extended Look was updated with confirmation that the content in the broadcast was "captured entirely from in-game footage on PlayStation 5." That's no surprise, either, as the May 2025 GTA 6 trailer was also captured on PlayStation 5, and not the PS5 Pro. Sony and Rockstar have a co-marketing agreement for GTA 6, which is why this is happening. It may also help explain why GTA 6 features consoles and controllers that resemble PlayStation's own devices. The Extended Look begins today at 12 PM PT / 3 PM ET, and while the broadcast will initially air on Netflix, it will come to YouTube at 6 PM PT / 9 PM ET. For more, be sure to read GameSpot's breakdown of how to watch and what to expect from the GTA 6 Extended Look event. The Netflix event comes after GTA 6 has suffered numerous, significant gameplay leaks. Rockstar reacted to the scandal, saying the leaks are "heartbreaking" for the developers. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's coming to market with an incredible amount of hype behind it, in part because fans have been waiting 13 years for the sequel to GTA 5.

title: Elden Ring’s Messmer The Impaler Actor Is Reportedly In The Running To Be The Next James Bond
description: Following the report that said Battlefield 1's Jack Lowden is circling the role of James Bond for the next 007 movie, it’s now rumored that another actor who appeared in a video game, Jack Barton, could be in the mix as well. PageSix reported that Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve and casting director Nina Gold are looking at a "stream of unknowns" to play James Bond next. One such person is Barton, who played Messmer the Impaler in Elden Ring's Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. That is Barton's only video game credit. On TV, he appeared in Steven Knight's SAS: Rogue Heroes and the TV show War of the Worlds. In film, Barton appeared in Yorgos Lanthimos' Oscar-winning 2023 movie Poor Things. The report went on to say Barton will do a screen test to play James Bond, as will other contenders, including Lowden. These tests will begin in early September and will also reportedly include people like Callum Turner, Jacob Elordi, Paul Mescal, and Harris Dickson. In May this year, Bond movie production company Amazon MGM Studios said the search for the next James Bond actor was underway and that the film studio would not comment on the casting process. It has been a long wait for the next James Bond movie, as the latest entry, No Time to Die, was released in 2021. However, it was expected to be release much sooner, but had three delays due in part to COVID. Daniel Craig played James Bond in five 007 films, and wrapped up his run with No Time To Die. Amazon MGM Studios bought the franchise and reportedly paid a lot of money to regain creative control from the longtime series stewards Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson. The new James Bond movie will be directed by Villeneuve, the Oscar-nominated filmmaker known for the Dune franchise. He’s also directed the movies Prisoners, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival.

title: Xbox Won’t Say If Project Helix Has A Disc Drive, But It’s Not Giving Up On Physical Games Yet
description: Sony has already confirmed that it's headed toward an all-digital future soon, but what about Xbox and its next-gen console, Project Helix? In a new interview, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma didn't give any concrete answers about whether Project Helix will have a disc drive, instead focusing on the topic of next-gen hardware affordability. "This next generation, we have to be thinking about efficiency and affordability alongside performance," Sharma said to the BBC. "All of the industry needs to start to innovate on affordability and efficiency. That is something that we have not had to do [previously]. But with the crisis that's currently happening in hardware and components, it is absolutely something all of us need to be thinking about, innovating on, and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console." On the topic of physical media, Sharma said her focus was on giving players choices for how they purchase their games. "I want to make sure people have a choice. There are stacks of games on everybody's shelves," she said. While Sony's pivot to digital has been poorly received so far, Xbox has been laying the groundwork for this shift away from physical games for several years now. Options like Smart Delivery, Play Anywhere, and the recently announced disc-to-digital program has helped make the transition easier while still giving Xbox owners the option to purchase physical games. In comparison, PlayStation owners will be limited to a single storefront run by Sony, one that currently doesn't offer consumer-friendly services like refunds or gifting, as Valve's Steam platform does. It's no wonder that the decision to go digital has been so unpopular and has resulted in a flood of negative comments whenever Sony posts anything online. Xbox, on the other hand, is primed to win a war of opinion if it offers some form of physical ownership of its games, even if that section of its market only makes up a tiny number of sales.…

title: GTA 6 Wants To Remind You That Looks Matter In The Influencer Hustle Of Vice City
description: Ahead of today's GTA 6 Extended Preview on Netflix, developer Rockstar Games has revealed plenty of new details on the highly anticipated open-world game. In a new interview, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson divulged how the game, similar to GTA: San Andreas, will require you to take good care of the protagonists Jason and Lucia, as the duo will need to engage in exercise, healthy eating, and relaxation if they want to stay in shape. Just like real life, but with more immediate gains. Getting physical First off, Jason and Lucia's physiques will change according to how you take care of them between missions. Working out will visibly build muscle for the pair, while gorging on food will make them get noticeably heavier. Rockstar says it wants to enable "self-expression" amongst players without losing "the essence" of the characters. On that topic, Jason is ex-military and a drug runner, while Lucia has just finished a stint in prison when GTA 6 starts. You'll also need to ensure that Jason and Lucia get some rest between their outings, as staying awake for several days or constantly evading the police will take a toll on them. Players will have the option to play as the couple or go solo in the game, and swapping between them is designed to be a seamless experience. "The thing we love about this medium is the way these characters aren’t empty avatars that you can do whatever you want with," Nelson said to Dazed (via Shinobi602 ). "Their story becomes a journey you share with them." Contrary to what your parents told you, looks do matter--especially in Vice City. Nelson says that Vice City is built around vanity, and how Jason and Lucia appear will "carry significant weight" as players interact with social media stars, celebrities, and tourists. Choice and consequences Rockstar is also aiming to make the world of GTA 6 more reactive to players, with repercussions for certain actions. Rockstar says that the consequences will "cut much deeper" than in previous…

title: Former PlayStation Studios President Praises Xbox’s Solution To A Digital-Only Future
description: Former President of PlayStation Studios, Shuhei Yoshida, has praised Microsoft's recently announced disc-to-digital program, writing that it is a "great move by team Xbox." The former executive posted his opinion on the program on X with no other commentary, but it's a notable remark given how much of Yoshida's career was spent at Xbox's main competitor. That's especially true when you consider the differences in approach Microsoft and Sony seem to be taking as we march towards an all-digital future, with Sony announcing that it plans to stop PlayStation disc production for new titles from January 2028. It, unlike Xbox, hasn't yet announced a method for current physical game owners to continue using their discs on a potentially digital-only PlayStation 6. Xbox's approach is relatively straightforward. After inserting a disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S console, you will be granted a digital license for the game which enables you to play it across Xbox, PC (where compatible), and Xbox Cloud Streaming without requiring the disc any longer. The catch is that if you happen to sell the disc or lend it to a friend, that digital license will be revoked from your profile and associated with any new one that makes use of the disc itself. It's a smart way to ensure your physical library is still playable in the case of a new Xbox shipping without a disc drive, for an example. Yoshida spent over 30 years working at Sony, eventually becoming President of SIE Worldwide Studios (now known as PlayStation Studios) from 2008 to 2019. Yoshida then became the head of PlayStation Indies before retiring in 2024. Earlier this year, Yoshida revealed that he'd been fired from his former presidential role for not listening to Jim Ryan, the former CEO and chairman of Sony Interactive Entertainment. Yoshida has remained vocal within the games industry, providing consulting services and appearing at conventions and conferences as a speaker. He recently discussed the role of AI in game…

If you're planning to watch--and you have a Netflix subscription--here's everything you need to know about the upcoming GTA 6 preview. When to watch on Netflix Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look will premiere on Netflix at the following times on August 27: 3 PM ET 12 PM PT 8 PM BST 9 PM CEST 10 PM SAST 12 AM GST (August 28) 5 AM JST (August 28) 7 AM AEST (August 28) When to watch on YouTube Following its six hours of Netflix exclusivity, the GTA preview will be available to watch on YouTube and the official GTA 6 website. 9 PM ET 6 PM PT 2 AM BST (August 28) 3 AM CEST (August 28) 4 AM SAST (August 28) 6 AM GST (August 28) 11 AM JST (August 28) 1 PM AEST (August 28) Netflix subscriptions: How much do they cost? While you absolutely do not need Netflix to watch the Extended Look--since it will be free on YouTube a few hours later--if you can't wait, there are several options available, ranging from ad-supported to pricier premium subscriptions. Netflix Standard with ads -- $9 per month Netflix Standard -- $20 per month Netflix Premium -- $27 per month What to expect Unsurprisingly, Rockstar Games is keeping mum on what will be shown during the preview-- but one leaker hasn't been dropping a ton of pilfered content lately. There's no word yet on how long the Extended Look will run for or what parts of the game it'll cover, but fans are expecting brand-new footage and a proper look at how GTA 6 will play. If it's anything like the previous games in the series, expect driving, shooting, and a closer look at Vice City.
